newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: OVERNIGHT GUILDERS COAST AT HIGHS.
newsitem.headline: OVERNIGHT GUILDERS COAST AT HIGHS.

text.p: Dutch money market activity focused on the short end during Wednesday trade, with call money rates holding onto their recent highs.
Traders said overnight guilders were traded at 3.25-31 percent, with the majority of deals changing hands at 3.31.
But dealers said the continued high level of call money rates need not mean a hike in the special advances rate when a new pact is announced on Thursday.
Call is customarily traded around the special advances rate, which is currently pegged at 3.0 percent.
"It's been higher than that for some time now," a dealer said, adding that guilder-mark parity also offered cause for rate hike speculation.
The guilder was officially pegged at 112.66 per 100 marks on Wednesday, close to its ERM central rate of 112.673. This represented a softening from Tuesday's 112.645 guilders per 100 marks.
But dealers said that while there were many arguments for a rise in the short-term liquidity rate, an independent move by the Dutch central bank on Thursday was not generally expected.
Demand in longer-dated paper was offset by little or no offering, dealers said, and one- to 12-month guilder rates remained unmoved at the previous day's levels.
